ui.lib.arcade.mustPass: You have no legal move — you pass.
ui.lib.arcade.noHint: No useful move left. Draw a card, deal a new row or start over.
ui.lib.arcade.note.2048: Use the arrow keys or swipe to slide every tile. Two tiles with the same number merge into one when they touch. Make a tile equal to the target to clear the level; if no tile can move, you lose.
ui.lib.arcade.note.blocks: Rotate and place the falling pieces to fill horizontal lines; full lines disappear. ← → move, ↑ rotates, ↓ soft drops, Space hard drops, P pauses. Clear the required number of lines to pass the level; if the stack reaches the top, you lose.
ui.lib.arcade.note.breakout: Move the mouse, drag your finger on the field or use ← → to steer the paddle and keep the ball in play. Break every brick to clear the level; bricks with a thick border take two hits. You have 3 lives. Press Space to start or pause.
ui.lib.arcade.note.connect4: You play red and move first. Tap a column to drop a disc; it falls to the lowest empty spot. The first to line up 4 discs horizontally, vertically or diagonally wins.
ui.lib.arcade.note.freecell: All cards are face up. Move all 52 cards to the 4 foundations by suit, from A to K. On the tableau, build down in alternating colors. The free cells at the top left hold one card each; how many cards you can move at once depends on the free cells and empty columns. Higher levels have fewer free cells.
ui.lib.arcade.note.gomoku: You play X and move first; the computer plays O. Take turns placing a mark on an empty point of the 15×15 board. The first to get 5 in a row horizontally, vertically or diagonally wins.
ui.lib.arcade.note.klondike: Move all 52 cards to the 4 foundations by suit, from A to K. On the tableau, build down in alternating colors; only a K can go into an empty column. Tap the face-down pile at the top left to draw. Tap a card and then where you want it, or tap the card again to send it to a valid spot. Levels 1–5 draw 1 card, levels 6–10 draw 3.
ui.lib.arcade.note.match3: Swap two neighboring pieces (tap one then the other, or swipe) to make a line of 3 or more of the same kind; the line pops and the pieces above fall down. Chain reactions multiply your points. Reach the target score before you run out of moves.
ui.lib.arcade.note.minesweeper: Tap a cell to open it. A number shows how many mines are in the 8 cells around it. Flag a suspected mine with a right click, a long press or Flag mode. Tap a number that already has enough flags around it to open the rest quickly. Open every cell without a mine to win.
ui.lib.arcade.note.reversi: You play Black and move first. Place a disc so that it traps one or more White discs between it and another Black disc (horizontally, vertically or diagonally); the trapped discs flip to your color. If you have no legal move, you pass. When the board is full, whoever has more discs wins.
ui.lib.arcade.note.snake: Steer the snake with the arrow keys, WASD, the buttons below or by swiping. Eat the red food to grow; reach the required length to pass the level. From level 3, hitting a wall ends the game; higher levels add obstacles. Don't bite your own tail.
ui.lib.arcade.note.spider: Build each suit into a run from K down to A on the tableau; a complete 13-card run is removed automatically. Any card can go on a card one rank higher, but only same-suit runs move together. When you're stuck, tap Deal a new row (every column must have cards). Levels 1–3 use one suit, 4–7 two suits, 8–10 four suits.
ui.lib.arcade.shuffled: No moves left — the board was reshuffled.
ui.lib.arcade.noHintFc: No useful move left. Try undoing a few moves or start over.
ui.lib.arcade.wrapOff: K does not link to A
ui.lib.arcade.hintDraw: No pairs left. Click the stock to draw.
ui.lib.arcade.note.blackjack: Play money only — no real money. You start with 500 chips; reach the target chip count within the allowed number of hands to clear the level. Get closer to 21 than the dealer without going over. The dealer draws until reaching 17. A blackjack (an ace plus a ten-value card) pays extra. Double: double your bet and take exactly one more card. Split: available when your first two cards have the same value.
ui.lib.arcade.note.videopoker: Play money only — no real money. Choose a bet of 1–5 chips, press Deal to get five cards, click the cards you want to keep, then press Draw to replace the rest. A pair of jacks or better pays. You start with 100 chips; reach the target chip count within the allowed number of hands to clear the level.
ui.lib.arcade.note.checkers: You play Red (bottom) and move first. A piece moves one square diagonally forward onto an empty square. If you can jump over an opposing piece you must, and you may keep jumping to capture several pieces. A piece that reaches the far row is crowned king and can move and capture backward too. You lose when you have no pieces or no legal move.
ui.lib.arcade.ckWin: Black has no legal moves — you win.
ui.lib.arcade.ckLose: You have no legal moves — you lose.
ui.lib.arcade.ckMust: You must capture when you can — pick one of the pulsing pieces.
ui.lib.arcade.note.oanquan: A traditional Vietnamese game. The bottom row is yours, the top row is the computer's, and the two ends are the Mandarin squares. Click one of your squares, then choose a direction: all stones in it are picked up and sown one per square. After sowing, if the next square has stones, pick them up and keep sowing; if the next square is empty and the one after it has stones or a Mandarin, you capture it (and keep capturing if another empty square is followed by a loaded one). Stop at a Mandarin square or after two empty squares in a row. A Mandarin is worth 10 points, a stone 1. If your side runs out of stones, 5 of your captured points are sown back. The game ends when both Mandarins are captured; the higher score wins.
ui.lib.arcade.oqWin: Game over — you have more points.
ui.lib.arcade.oqLose: Game over — the computer has more points.
ui.lib.arcade.note.ludo: You play Red; the other colours are played by the computer. Roll the die: you need a 6 to bring a token out of its yard, and a 6 gives you another roll (three 6s in a row loses your turn). Tokens travel clockwise around the board, then turn into the home column of their colour; you need the exact number to reach the finish in the centre. Landing exactly on an opponent's token sends it back to its yard (except on star squares and start squares). The first player to bring all 4 tokens home wins.
ui.lib.arcade.ldWin: All 4 of your tokens are home!
ui.lib.arcade.threeSix: Three 6s in a row — you lose your turn.
ui.lib.arcade.note.pyramid: Clear all 28 cards of the pyramid. Click two free cards (not covered by any card) that add up to 13 (A=1, J=11, Q=12) to remove both; a King is removed alone with one click. The top card of the waste pile can be used too. Click the stock to draw; the number of times you can recycle the waste pile is limited.
ui.lib.arcade.note.tripeaks: Clear all 28 cards of the three peaks. Click a free card that is exactly one rank higher or lower than the card showing on the waste pile (any suit) to move it down. When you are out of moves, click the stock to draw. On the easier levels, a King links to an Ace.
ui.lib.arcade.note.golf: Press on the course, pull back away from where you want to hit (like a slingshot) and release to strike the ball; the farther you pull, the harder the hit. Sink the ball in the hole when it is slow enough; sand slows it down. Each level is a different course with a limited number of strokes.
ui.lib.arcade.hnBad: You cannot place a larger disc on a smaller one.
ui.lib.arcade.fillAll: Please pick a colour for every position.
ui.lib.arcade.note.nonogram: The numbers at the start of each row and column give the lengths of the runs of consecutive filled cells in that line, in order, with at least one empty cell between runs. Click or drag to fill cells; switch to “Mark ✕” to note cells you are sure are empty. Satisfy every clue to win.
ui.lib.arcade.note.sokoban: Move the player with the arrow keys/WASD, the buttons below, or by swiping. Push every box onto a goal square (the round dots). You can only push one box at a time and cannot pull, so avoid pushing boxes into corners. Use Undo to fix a bad move.
ui.lib.arcade.note.block10: Pick a piece at the bottom, then click the grid to place it (pieces cannot be rotated). Fill a whole row or column to clear it and score extra points; clearing several lines at once earns a big bonus. Reach the target score to clear the level; if none of the remaining pieces fits, you lose.
ui.lib.arcade.note.dots: Take turns joining two neighbouring dots with a line. Whoever draws the fourth side of a square claims it (in their colour) and moves again. When all lines are drawn, the player with more squares wins. Avoid drawing the third side of a square, or your opponent will take it.
ui.lib.arcade.note.ultimate: The board is made of 9 small tic-tac-toe boards. You play X and go first. The cell you pick inside a small board decides which small board your opponent must play in next (it is highlighted); if that board is already finished, they may play anywhere. Win a small board to claim it; claim three small boards in a row, column or diagonal to win the game.
ui.lib.arcade.note.lights-out: Clicking a cell toggles that cell and its 4 neighbours (on/off). Turn all the lights off. Use Hint to see a cell worth pressing.
ui.lib.arcade.note.fifteen: Slide the numbered tiles into the gap to put them in order 1, 2, 3… with the gap in the bottom-right corner. Click a tile in the same row or column as the gap to slide the whole line; arrow keys also work.
ui.lib.arcade.note.flood-it: Pick a colour to fill the whole area you own in the top-left corner; it swallows neighbouring cells of that colour. Make the entire board one colour within the allowed number of moves.
ui.lib.arcade.note.mastermind: The computer hides a row of colours. Choose a colour for each position, then press Guess. A black peg = right colour in the right place; a white peg = right colour in the wrong place. Crack the code before you run out of guesses.
ui.lib.arcade.note.hanoi: Move all the discs to the last peg. Move only the top disc of a peg each time, and never place a larger disc on a smaller one. Click the source peg, then the target peg.
ui.lib.arcade.note.pipes: Click a tile to rotate the pipe 90°. Connect every pipe into one network with no open ends left (open ends are shown in red).
ui.lib.arcade.note.whack-a-mole: Moles pop up from the holes — click or tap a mole to whack it. Whack enough moles before time runs out. From level 4 there are bombs: hitting one costs you points.
ui.lib.arcade.note.simon: The game plays a sequence of colours and sounds — repeat it in the same order. Each round adds one more step. Remember the required length to clear the level. From level 7 there are 6 pads.
ui.lib.arcade.note.aim-trainer: Targets appear at random and vanish quickly — hit as many as you can. They get smaller and faster. Hit enough targets before more than 5 misses to clear the level.
ui.lib.arcade.note.quick-math: Solve in your head as fast as you can: type the answer and press Enter. Each question has a time limit; a wrong answer or timeout costs a life (you have 3). Answer enough questions correctly to clear the level.
ui.lib.arcade.note.reaction: Wait for the screen to turn green, then click as fast as you can. Clicking too early is a foul (3 fouls and you lose). Your average over 5 rounds must beat the level’s limit.
ui.lib.arcade.note.pong: Move the mouse, drag your finger or use the ← → keys to control the bottom paddle. Knock the ball past the computer; first to 5 points wins. The ball speeds up with every hit.
ui.lib.arcade.note.space-shooter: Move the mouse, drag your finger or use the ← → keys to steer; your ship fires automatically. Destroy enough enemy ships to clear the level, and avoid collisions and enemy fire. You have 3 lives.
ui.lib.arcade.note.asteroids: ← → rotate the ship, ↑ thrusts, Space fires. Destroy every rock to clear the level; big rocks split into smaller ones. The ship wraps around the screen edges. You have 3 lives.
ui.lib.arcade.note.maze: Use the arrow keys (or swipe, or the buttons) to get from the green dot to the red flag before time runs out. From level 5 the maze is foggy: you only see around you, and visited areas are remembered.
ui.lib.arcade.note.road-cross: Use the arrow keys, swipe or the buttons to hop the frog from bottom to top. Avoid the traffic; from level 5 the upper part is a river, so hop onto the floating logs. Get home 3 times to clear the level. You have 3 lives.
ui.lib.arcade.note.flappy: Tap the play area, press Space or ↑ to flap. Fly through the gaps between pipes without touching a pipe, the ground or the ceiling. Higher levels have narrower gaps and faster flight.
ui.lib.arcade.note.runner: Tap the play area, press Space or ↑ to jump over cacti; hold ↓ to duck under high birds (or jump over low ones). Run far enough to clear the level. The speed keeps rising.
ui.lib.arcade.note.kalah: You play the bottom row, the computer the top; the big pit on the right is your store. Click a pit to pick up all its seeds and sow them counter-clockwise, one per pit (skipping your opponent’s store). If your last seed lands in your store you move again; if it lands in an empty pit on your side opposite a pit with seeds, you capture those seeds. When one side is empty, the other side’s seeds go to its owner’s store; the bigger store wins.
ui.lib.arcade.note.snakes: Roll the die and move that many squares, from 1 up to 100. Land on the foot of a ladder to climb it, or on a snake’s head to slide down. From level 4 you must roll the exact number to land on 100. Higher levels have more snakes, fewer ladders and more opponents. First to reach 100 wins.
ui.lib.arcade.needExact: You need the exact number to land on 100.
ui.lib.arcade.note.nmm: Each side has 9 pieces. Phase 1: take turns placing pieces on empty points. Phase 2: slide a piece to an adjacent empty point. With only 3 pieces left you may “fly” to any empty point. Make three in a row (a “mill”) to remove an opponent’s piece (pieces not in a mill first). You lose when you are down to 2 pieces or cannot move. You play white and go first.
ui.lib.arcade.removePiece: Pick an opponent piece to remove.
ui.lib.arcade.note.battleship: Each side has 5 ships (lengths 5, 4, 3, 3, 2) placed at random on a 10x10 grid. Take turns firing at a cell: a hit turns red, a miss turns light blue, and hitting every cell of a ship sinks it. Sink the whole enemy fleet first to win. At higher levels the computer deduces your ships’ positions more cleverly.
ui.lib.arcade.theySunk: The enemy sank one of your ships!
ui.lib.arcade.theyHit: The enemy hit one of your ships.
ui.lib.arcade.note.bau-cua: Virtual coins only — no real money. Pick a chip value, click the animals to place bets, then press Shake. For every die that matches an animal you bet on, you get your stake back plus an equal amount for each match. Reach the target coins within the allowed rounds to clear the level.
ui.lib.arcade.note.baccarat: Virtual coins only — no real money. Bet on Player, Banker or Tie, then press Deal. A hand’s value is the last digit of its total (A = 1, 2–9 face value, 10/J/Q/K = 0); the hand closer to 9 wins, and third cards are drawn by the standard rules. Player pays 1:1, Banker 0.95:1, Tie 8:1 (Player/Banker bets are returned on a tie). Reach the target coins within the allowed rounds to clear the level.
ui.lib.arcade.note.bai-cao: Virtual coins only — no real money. Each side gets 3 cards. A hand scores the last digit of its total (A = 1, 2–9 face value, 10/J/Q/K = 10, i.e. 0 points). Ranking: Three of a kind (“Sáp”) is highest, then three face cards (“Ba tiên”), then 9 points down to 0. Place a bet, press Deal and then Reveal to compare with the dealer. From level 6 the dealer wins ties. Reach the target coins within the allowed rounds to clear the level.
ui.lib.arcade.note.bingo: The computer calls numbers from 1 to 75. When a called number is on your card, click it to mark it (the centre is free). Complete a row, column or diagonal and press BINGO! — you must beat the computer opponents. A false BINGO! locks the button for a few seconds. Higher levels call faster and have more opponents.
ui.lib.arcade.falseBingo: Not a full line yet! Button locked for 3 seconds.
ui.lib.arcade.note.yahtzee: Each turn you roll 5 dice up to 3 times: click a die to keep it, then press Roll to re-roll the others. Then pick a box in the table to score (each box is used once; a box that does not fit scores 0). 13 turns. The Ones–Sixes boxes add a 35 bonus if they total 63 or more. Reach the level’s target score to win.
ui.lib.arcade.note.crazy-eights: Play a card that matches the top card of the discard pile by suit or rank. Eights are wild: play one any time and choose a new suit. If you have no playable card, draw from the pile (up to 3 cards); if you still cannot play, you pass. First to empty their hand wins. Higher levels have more opponents and the computer plays more cleverly.
ui.lib.arcade.mustPlay: You have a playable card — play it.
ui.lib.arcade.note.race: Press ← → (or tap the lane you want) to change lanes and dodge the cars ahead. You have 3 lives; drive the full distance to clear the level. Higher levels add lanes and faster traffic.
ui.lib.arcade.note.jump: The character bounces by itself. Press ← → or drag your finger to land on the next platform. Blue platforms move, brown ones break when you land. Falling off the screen loses; climb high enough to clear the level.
ui.lib.arcade.note.miner: The hook swings back and forth; press Space, ↓ or tap the field to drop it. Big gold and rocks are heavy and pull slowly; diamonds are worth a lot. Reach the target money before the 60 seconds run out.
ui.lib.arcade.note.slicer: Swipe a finger or the mouse across the fruit to slice it. Avoid the black bombs. Missing a fruit or slicing a bomb costs a life (you have 3). Slice enough fruit to clear the level.
ui.lib.arcade.note.hoops: Press on the court, drag down (like a slingshot) and release to shoot the ball at the hoop. The farther you drag, the harder the throw. Score enough baskets within the shots you have; from level 4 the hoop moves.
ui.lib.arcade.note.bubbles: Move the mouse or finger to aim, then click/tap or press Space/Fire to shoot. Connect 3 or more bubbles of the same color to pop them; bubbles that lose their support fall. The rows slowly drop, so keep them away from the bottom line. Clear all bubbles to win.
ui.lib.arcade.note.chase: Use the arrow keys (or swipe / the buttons) to turn and eat every dot in the maze while avoiding the ghosts chasing you. You have 3 lives; higher levels add more ghosts that are faster and chase smarter.
ui.lib.arcade.note.kakuro: Fill the white cells with digits 1–9 so that each run adds up to the clue in the black cell (the number at the top right is for the run to the right, the one at the bottom left for the run below), with no digit repeated within a run. Use the arrow keys to move.
ui.lib.arcade.note.kenken: Fill the grid with the numbers 1 to N so that no number repeats in any row or column. Each heavily outlined cage shows a target and an operation (+, −, ×, ÷): the numbers in the cage must give that result. Use the arrow keys to move.
ui.lib.arcade.note.wordGuess: Guess the secret English word. After each try, green means the right letter in the right place, yellow means the letter is in the word but elsewhere, and gray means it is not in the word. Type on your keyboard or use the on-screen keys, and press Enter to submit. Higher levels have longer words and fewer tries.
ui.lib.arcade.note.hangman: Guess the secret English word by picking letters one at a time. Each wrong letter adds a part to the hanged figure; when you run out of wrong guesses you lose. Higher levels have longer words and fewer wrong guesses allowed.
ui.lib.arcade.note.scramble: Rearrange the scrambled letters into a real English word and type it in the answer box. Each level has 5 words; solve at least 4 before each word’s timer runs out to clear the level. The hint reveals the first letter.
ui.lib.arcade.note.domino: Each player gets 7 tiles; whoever holds the highest double starts. Play a tile whose number matches one end of the chain. If you cannot play, draw from the boneyard until you can; if it is empty, pass. First to empty their hand wins; if both are blocked, the lower pip total wins.
ui.lib.arcade.note.hearts: Four players, 13 cards each. The 2 of clubs leads. You must follow the suit led if you can. Each heart is 1 point and the Queen of Spades is 13; whoever wins a trick takes its points. Lower is better, and taking all 26 points gives everyone else 26 instead. You cannot lead a heart until one has been played. After the last hand, you win if your score is the lowest (or tied for lowest).
ui.lib.arcade.note.holdem: Heads-up against the computer using virtual chips only. Each player gets 2 private cards and 5 community cards are revealed (flop, turn, river); make the best 5-card hand. Each round you can fold, call (or check) or raise. The blinds rise every 4 hands. You win when the computer runs out of chips, or by having more chips after the hand limit. No real money is involved.
ui.lib.arcade.hrIllegal: You cannot play this card (follow the suit, or no hearts lead yet).
ui.lib.arcade.thOppFold: The computer folds; you win this hand.
ui.lib.arcade.note.nback: A square lights up one after another on a 3x3 grid. Press "Match!" (or Space) when the lit position is the same as the one N steps ago (N is shown above). You need at least 80% correct decisions to clear the level. Higher levels use a larger N.
ui.lib.arcade.note.clicker: Click the cookie to bake cookies, then spend them on helpers that bake automatically (prices rise with each one you buy). Bake the target number of cookies within 2 minutes to clear the level.
ui.lib.arcade.note.onet: Select two identical tiles that can be joined by a path with at most 2 turns that does not cross other tiles to remove them. Clear all the tiles before time runs out to win. When no moves are left you can shuffle (limited uses).
ui.lib.arcade.note.jigsaw: The picture is cut into pieces and shuffled. Tap one piece, then another, to swap them, and rebuild the picture shown as the reference. Pieces in the right place get a green border. Higher levels have more pieces.
ui.lib.arcade.note.backgammon: You play the white checkers, moving from the top right around to the bottom right (your home). Roll the dice, click the checker you want to move, then click a highlighted destination. Landing on a point with exactly one opposing checker hits it onto the middle bar, and that player must bring it back in first. You cannot land on a point with two or more opposing checkers. Once all 15 of your checkers are in your home board (the last 6 points) you may bear them off. The first to bear off all 15 wins.
ui.lib.arcade.youNoMove: You have no legal move left.
ui.lib.arcade.note.tienlen: Four players, 13 cards each. Card order from low to high: 3, 4, … K, A, 2; suits from low to high: spades, clubs, diamonds, hearts. Whoever holds the 3 of spades goes first. Play a single card, a pair, three of a kind, four of a kind, or a run of 3 or more consecutive cards (no 2s). The next player must play the same type and higher, or pass; four of a kind can beat a single 2 or a pair of 2s. When everyone else passes, the last player to play may lead anything. First to empty their hand wins. Select cards, then press Play.
ui.lib.arcade.tlFree: Table empty — you may lead anything
ui.lib.arcade.tlBad: The selected cards do not form a valid set.
ui.lib.arcade.tlLow: This set is not high enough to beat the table.
ui.lib.arcade.note.td: Tap an empty square (not the path) to build a shooting tower, which costs gold; tap a tower again to upgrade it (up to level 5). Towers automatically shoot the enemy that has gone farthest within range. Defeat enemies to earn more gold; if 15 enemies reach the end you lose. Survive every wave to clear the level.
ui.lib.arcade.note.colorNum: Every square has a number matching a color in the palette. Pick a color, then tap the squares with that number to paint them; tapping with the wrong color paints nothing. Paint every square correctly to finish the picture. Higher levels have more colors.
ui.lib.arcade.cnWrong: Wrong color — check the number on the square.
ui.lib.arcade.note.yukon: Like Klondike but with no stock: any face-up card can be moved together with every card on top of it, even if they are not in sequence; only the first card must fit the target column (descending, alternating red and black; a King goes to an empty column). Build all 52 cards up on the four foundations from Ace to King. Low levels start with more cards already face up.
ui.lib.arcade.note.chinesechk: You play the blue pieces in the right-hand corner; move all 10 of them to the opposite left-hand corner before the computer does. Each turn you move one piece: step to an empty neighbouring hole, or jump over any piece to the empty hole right behind it, and keep jumping as many times as you like. Tap one of your pieces, then tap a green hole to move.
ui.lib.arcade.ccDraw: Out of turns — it is a draw.
ui.lib.arcade.note.maubinh: You and the computer each get 13 cards and arrange them into 3 hands: a 5-card back hand, a 5-card middle hand and a 3-card front hand. The back hand must be at least as strong as the middle, and the middle at least as strong as the front; otherwise your arrangement is fouled and you lose the whole round. Tap a card, then tap the row where it goes (tap a placed card to take it back). Each hand you win scores 1 point; winning all 3 scores 6. Play 5 rounds — a positive total clears the level. The front hand can only be high card, a pair or three of a kind.
ui.lib.arcade.mbAutoMsg: Here is a suggested arrangement. You can change it before showing the cards.
ui.lib.arcade.note.phom: Two players; each gets 9 cards (whoever goes first gets 10). A meld is 3 or more cards of the same rank, or 3 or more consecutive cards of the same suit (Ace is only low). On your turn draw a card from the deck, or take the card your opponent just discarded if it forms a meld with your hand (a card you took must be kept), then discard one card. When each player has discarded 4 cards the round ends and whoever has the lower total of unmelded cards (Ace = 1 … King = 13) wins. If all your cards are in melds after a discard you go out ("U") and win at once. Cards outlined in green are in your best set of melds.
ui.lib.arcade.pmAte: You took this card — keep it in a meld.
ui.lib.arcade.pmKeep: A card you took must be kept — discard another.
ui.lib.arcade.note.shogi: Shogi is Japanese chess. You play the lower side and move first; the computer's pieces point the other way. Captured pieces go into your hand and can be dropped on any empty square instead of making a move (never a pawn in a file where you already have an unpromoted pawn, and never a piece on a rank where it could not move again). A piece that moves into, out of, or within the last three ranks of the opponent may promote (except King and Gold); promotion is forced when a piece would have no moves. Checkmate the enemy King to win. Kanji: 歩 pawn, 香 lance, 桂 knight, 銀 silver, 金 gold, 角 bishop, 飛 rook, 玉 king; と, 馬, 竜 and other red pieces are promoted.
ui.lib.arcade.note.janggi: Janggi is Korean chess. You play the blue pieces at the bottom and move first. Unlike xiangqi there is no river, and both palaces have diagonal lines. The General and Guards move one step along the palace lines (diagonals included); the Chariot also slides and captures along palace diagonals; the Cannon must jump over exactly one piece (not another Cannon) to move or capture, and cannot capture a Cannon; the Horse steps one point straight then one diagonally, and the Elephant one straight then two diagonally, both blocked if a piece is in the way; Soldiers move forward or sideways, and diagonally forward inside the enemy palace. The two Generals may never face each other. Checkmate the enemy General to win. The computer never passes.

go-game.desc: Play Go against the computer across 10 levels, or online on 9x9, 13x13 and 19x19 boards with a friend or a new opponent. Automatic scoring at the end.

memory-shapes.name: Shape & Colour Memory
memory-shapes.desc: Tiles with shapes and colours are shown for 5 seconds, then hidden; remember and pick the right tile, 10 levels from easy to hard.

web-desktop.name: Online Desktop
web-desktop.desc: A computer desktop in your browser: file manager, Notepad, image and PDF viewer, calculator, calendar and trash. Files are saved to your Google Drive.

co-up.name: Dark Chess
co-up.desc: Play Vietnamese dark Xiangqi: pieces start face down and flip after their first move. Play the computer across 10 levels or play online with friends or new opponents.

game-2048.desc: Slide and merge matching numbers to build the 2048 tile; 10 levels with targets from 64 to 8192, with undo.

minesweeper.name: Minesweeper
minesweeper.desc: Classic Minesweeper: open cells, place flags and work out where the mines are from the numbers; 10 levels from 8x8 to 18x18, works on phones.

block-puzzle.name: Falling Blocks
block-puzzle.desc: Rotate and stack falling blocks to clear lines; 10 levels of increasing speed, play with the keyboard or touch buttons.

snake.name: Snake
snake.desc: Steer the snake to eat and grow while avoiding walls and your own tail; 10 levels of increasing speed with obstacles.

solitaire.name: Solitaire
solitaire.desc: Classic Klondike Solitaire: build down in alternating colors and move cards to the foundations from A to K; draw 1 or 3, with undo and hints.

spider-solitaire.name: Spider Solitaire
spider-solitaire.desc: Spider Solitaire with 1, 2 and 4 suits: build same-suit runs from K to A to clear them off the table; 10 levels with undo and hints.

freecell.name: FreeCell
freecell.desc: FreeCell Solitaire: every card is face up; use the free cells to move cards to the foundations; 10 levels with fewer free cells as you go.

gomoku.name: Gomoku (Five in a Row)
gomoku.desc: Play Gomoku, five in a row, against the computer on a 15x15 board; 10 levels from easy to hard, with undo.

reversi.name: Reversi
reversi.desc: Trap your opponent's discs to flip them to your color; play 8x8 Reversi against the computer across 10 levels.

connect-four.name: Four in a Row
connect-four.desc: Drop discs into columns and line up 4 in a row horizontally, vertically or diagonally before the computer; 10 levels from easy to hard.

match-3.name: Match 3
match-3.desc: Swap candies to match 3 or more of a kind and set off chain reactions; 10 levels with a target score and a move limit.

brick-breaker.name: Brick Breaker
brick-breaker.desc: Steer the paddle and bounce the ball to break every brick; 10 stages with different layouts, play with mouse, touch or keys.

pyramid.name: Pyramid Solitaire
pyramid.desc: Clear the 28-card pyramid by pairing cards that add up to 13; 10 levels with fewer and fewer redeals.

tripeaks.name: TriPeaks Solitaire
tripeaks.desc: Clear three peaks by linking cards one rank apart; 10 levels from easy to hard.

golf.name: Golf Solitaire
golf.desc: Clear the columns by linking cards one rank apart from the showing card; 10 levels with more columns as you go.

blackjack.name: Blackjack
blackjack.desc: Play blackjack against the dealer with virtual chips: get closest to 21 without going over; double down and split; 10 levels with rising chip targets.

video-poker.name: Video Poker
video-poker.desc: Five-card draw poker with virtual chips (Jacks or Better); 10 levels with tighter pay tables.

checkers.name: Checkers
checkers.desc: Play 8x8 checkers against the computer: forced captures, multi-jumps and kings; 10 levels from easy to hard.

ludo.name: Ludo
ludo.desc: Four-colour race game: roll the die and bring your 4 tokens home first; play against 1 to 3 computer players over 10 levels.

o-an-quan.name: O An Quan
o-an-quan.desc: A traditional Vietnamese sowing game: sow stones and capture the Mandarins against the computer; 10 levels from easy to hard.

lights-out.name: Lights Out
lights-out.desc: Turn off every light: each press flips that cell and its 4 neighbours; 10 levels with growing boards and a hint button.

fifteen.name: 15 Puzzle (Sliding Puzzle)
fifteen.desc: Slide the numbered tiles into order; 10 levels from 3x3 to 5x5, played with mouse, touch or arrow keys.

flood-it.name: Flood-it
flood-it.desc: Flood the board from the corner until it is one colour within a limited number of moves; 10 levels with bigger boards and more colours.

mastermind.name: Mastermind (Code Breaker)
mastermind.desc: Crack the hidden colour code using black and white peg clues; 10 levels with longer codes and more colours.

hanoi.name: Tower of Hanoi
hanoi.desc: Move the discs from the first peg to the last without placing a larger disc on a smaller one; 10 levels from 3 discs to 12 discs on 4 pegs.

pipes.name: Pipe Connect
pipes.desc: Rotate the pipe pieces to join them into one network with no open ends; 10 levels with growing boards.

nonogram.name: Nonogram (Picross)
nonogram.desc: Fill cells using the number clues at the rows and columns to reveal a picture; 10 levels from 5x5 to 15x15.

sokoban.name: Sokoban (Box Pusher)
sokoban.desc: Push the boxes onto the goal squares in a warehouse; every level is solvable, with 10 levels of more boxes and bigger warehouses.

block-10x10.name: Block Puzzle 10x10
block-10x10.desc: Place pieces on a 10x10 grid and fill rows or columns to clear them and reach the target score; 10 levels.

dots-boxes.name: Dots and Boxes
dots-boxes.desc: Take turns joining dots to claim squares and beat the computer over 10 levels from easy to hard.

ultimate-tictactoe.name: Ultimate Tic-Tac-Toe
ultimate-tictactoe.desc: Tic-tac-toe across 9 small boards: the cell you choose decides where your opponent must play; vs the computer over 10 levels.

pong.name: Pong
pong.desc: Knock the ball past the computer; first to 5 points wins. 10 levels with a faster, sharper opponent.

space-shooter.name: Space Shooter
space-shooter.desc: Steer your ship, shoot down enemy ships and dodge their fire; 10 levels with bigger waves, return fire and tougher enemies.

asteroids.name: Asteroids
asteroids.desc: Rotate, thrust and shoot to break up the space rocks; big rocks split into smaller ones. 10 levels with more and faster rocks.

maze.name: Maze
maze.desc: Find your way out of the maze before time runs out; 10 levels from small to large mazes, with fog at higher levels.

road-cross.name: Road Crossing (Frogger-style)
road-cross.desc: Hop the frog across busy roads and rivers of floating logs to get home 3 times; 10 levels with faster traffic and a river at higher levels.

flappy.name: Flappy Bird-style Game
flappy.desc: Tap to flap and fly through the gaps between pipes; 10 levels with narrower gaps and rising speed.

runner.name: Dino Runner
runner.desc: Jump over cacti and duck under birds; run far enough to clear each of the 10 levels as the speed keeps rising.

whack-a-mole.name: Whack-a-Mole
whack-a-mole.desc: Whack the moles popping out of the holes before time runs out, and avoid the bombs; 10 levels from slow to very fast.

simon.name: Simon (Memory Colours)
simon.desc: Remember and repeat the sequence of colours and sounds; longer sequences over 10 levels, with 6 pads from level 7.

aim-trainer.name: Aim Trainer
aim-trainer.desc: Hit the targets that appear at random and vanish quickly; targets shrink over 10 levels, and your reaction time is measured.

quick-math.name: Quick Math
quick-math.desc: Do addition, subtraction, multiplication and division in your head under time pressure; 10 levels from simple sums to expressions.

reaction.name: Reaction Time Test
reaction.desc: Click the moment the screen turns green; your 5-round average must meet each level’s limit, which gets tighter over 10 levels.

kalah.name: Kalah (Mancala)
kalah.desc: Sow seeds around the pits, capture your opponent’s seeds and move again when you land in your store; play the computer over 10 levels from easy to hard.

snakes-ladders.name: Snakes and Ladders
snakes-ladders.desc: Roll the die from square 1 to 100, climb ladders, avoid snakes and reach the finish before your opponents; 10 levels.

nine-mens-morris.name: Nine Men’s Morris
nine-mens-morris.desc: Place, slide and fly your pieces to make three in a row and remove your opponent’s pieces; play the computer over 10 levels.

battleship.name: Battleship
battleship.desc: Find and sink the computer’s fleet on a 10x10 grid before it sinks yours; 10 levels as the computer deduces more cleverly.

bau-cua.name: Bầu Cua (Gourd Crab Fish Prawn)
bau-cua.desc: Traditional Vietnamese dice game: bet virtual coins on the animals and shake three dice; reach the target coins over 10 levels (no real money).

baccarat.name: Baccarat
baccarat.desc: Bet on Player, Banker or Tie with cards dealt by the standard rules, using virtual coins; reach the target coins over 10 levels (no real money).

bai-cao.name: Bài Cào (Three-Card Game)
bai-cao.desc: Compare 3-card hands with the dealer: three of a kind, three face cards, then 9 points down to 0; virtual coins, 10 levels, no real money.

bingo.name: Bingo
bingo.desc: Mark the called numbers on your 5x5 card and shout BINGO before the computer opponents; numbers are called faster over 10 levels.

yahtzee.name: Yahtzee (Five Dice)
yahtzee.desc: Roll five dice, keep the good ones and fill 13 scoring boxes; reach the target score over 10 levels.

crazy-eights.name: Crazy Eights
crazy-eights.desc: Match suit or rank, eights change the suit; empty your hand before 1 to 3 computer opponents over 10 levels.

car-race.name: Car Race Dodge
car-race.desc: Change lanes to dodge the cars ahead and drive the full distance; 10 levels with more lanes and faster traffic.

sky-jump.name: Sky Jump
sky-jump.desc: Bounce from platform to platform to climb as high as you can without falling; 10 levels with sparser platforms, moving ones and breakable ones.

gold-miner.name: Gold Miner
gold-miner.desc: Drop the hook to haul in gold and diamonds, avoid heavy rocks, and reach the target money within 60 seconds; 10 levels.

fruit-slice.name: Fruit Slice
fruit-slice.desc: Swipe to slice the fruit flying up and dodge the bombs; 10 levels with more fruit and more bombs.

basketball.name: Basketball Shoot
basketball.desc: Drag and release to shoot the ball into the hoop within a limited number of shots; 10 levels, with a moving hoop from level 4.

bubble-shooter.name: Bubble Shooter
bubble-shooter.desc: Shoot bubbles to connect 3 or more of the same color and pop them, and clear them all before they reach the bottom; 10 levels with more colors.

dot-chase.name: Dot Chase
dot-chase.desc: Eat every dot in the maze while dodging the ghosts that chase you; 10 levels with more and smarter ghosts.

kakuro.name: Kakuro (Cross Sums)
kakuro.desc: Fill the white cells with digits 1–9 so each run adds up to its clue with no repeats; 10 levels, grids from 5x5 to 9x9.

kenken.name: KenKen (Calcudoku)
kenken.desc: Fill the grid with no repeats in rows or columns so every cage gives its target with its operation; 10 levels, grids from 3x3 to 6x6.

word-guess.name: Word Guess (Wordle-style)
word-guess.desc: Guess the secret English word with green, yellow and gray hints; 10 levels with 4–6 letter words and fewer tries.

hangman.name: Hangman
hangman.desc: Guess the English word one letter at a time before you run out of wrong guesses; 10 levels with longer words and fewer wrong guesses.

word-scramble.name: Word Scramble (Anagram)
word-scramble.desc: Rearrange scrambled letters into an English word before time runs out; 10 levels, 5 words per level.

domino.name: Dominoes
domino.desc: Match tiles to either end of the chain and empty your hand before the computer; 10 levels as the computer gets smarter.

hearts.name: Hearts
hearts.desc: Avoid hearts and the Queen of Spades in a four-player card game; lower score is better; 10 levels against smarter computer players.

texas-holdem.name: Texas Hold'em (virtual chips)
texas-holdem.desc: Heads-up poker against the computer with virtual chips: fold, call or raise, and win when the computer runs out of chips; 10 levels, no real money.

n-back.name: N-Back Memory
n-back.desc: Watch the lit square and press Match when it is the same as N steps ago; 10 levels with N up to 4.

cookie-clicker.name: Cookie Clicker
cookie-clicker.desc: Click to bake cookies, buy helpers that bake automatically and reach the target within 2 minutes; 10 levels.

tile-connect.name: Tile Connect (Onet-style)
tile-connect.desc: Join matching tiles with a path of at most two turns and clear the board before time runs out; 10 levels, bigger boards.

jigsaw.name: Picture Jigsaw
jigsaw.desc: Swap the shuffled pieces to rebuild the picture; 10 levels from 3x3 to 6x6 pieces.

mini-golf.name: Mini Golf
mini-golf.desc: Pull back and release to putt the ball into the hole within the stroke limit; 10 courses with walls and sand.

backgammon.name: Backgammon
backgammon.desc: Roll the dice, race your checkers home and bear them off before the computer, hitting its blots on the way; 10 levels.

tien-len.name: Tiến Lên (Thirteen)
tien-len.desc: The Vietnamese shedding card game for four: play singles, pairs, runs and fours to empty your hand first; 10 levels.

tower-defense.name: Tower Defense
tower-defense.desc: Build and upgrade towers along the path to stop every wave of enemies; 10 levels on three different maps.

color-by-number.name: Color by Number
color-by-number.desc: Paint each square with the color that matches its number to reveal the picture; 10 pictures with more colors each time.

yukon.name: Yukon Solitaire
yukon.desc: Klondike without the stock: move any face-up card with everything on top of it; 10 levels, fewer cards face up as you go.

chinese-checkers.name: Chinese Checkers
chinese-checkers.desc: Star-shaped hop-and-step game against the computer: move all 10 pieces to the opposite corner first; 10 levels.

mau-binh.name: Mau Binh (Chinese Poker)
mau-binh.desc: Arrange 13 cards into three hands of 5, 5 and 3 cards and beat the computer; 5 rounds per level, 10 levels.

phom.name: Phom (Vietnamese Rummy)
phom.desc: Two-player Vietnamese rummy against the computer: draw or take a discard, form melds and go out; lowest leftover points wins; 10 levels.

shogi.name: Shogi (Japanese Chess)
shogi.desc: Play shogi against the computer: drop captured pieces, promote, and checkmate the king; 10 levels with undo.

janggi.name: Janggi (Korean Chess)
janggi.desc: Play Korean chess against the computer: palace diagonals, one-piece cannon jumps, three-step elephants; 10 levels with undo.

rsa-keys.note: Everything runs in your browser via Web Crypto and is never sent anywhere. Because RSA can only encrypt very short data directly, the tool uses hybrid encryption: it generates a random AES key to encrypt the text, then wraps that AES key with RSA — so text of any length can be encrypted. The recipient needs the matching private key to decrypt. The public key (SPKI) can be shared; the private key (PKCS#8) must be kept secret.

rsa-keys.err.pubRead: Could not read the public key. It needs the correct public PEM format (-----BEGIN PUBLIC KEY-----, SPKI).
rsa-keys.err.privRead: Could not read the private key. It needs the correct private PEM format (-----BEGIN PRIVATE KEY-----, PKCS#8).
rsa-keys.status.noPub: No public key, so cannot encrypt. Generate or paste a public key.
